title: Gor Says Big Items Done as India-US Trade Deal Nears Landing
excerpt: The ambassador said negotiators are down to product-level percentages, while a US decision on Russian oil sanctions affecting India is due within days.
body:
• US Ambassador Sergio Gor said on Thursday the major issues in the India-US trade deal are resolved, with talks now at product-by-product detail.
  • Gor gave no date for a final agreement and did not name the remaining sticking points.
  • A separate decision is due within about 10 days on whether new US sanctions powers over buyers of Russian oil and gas will affect India.
  • For Indian exporters and US importers, the earlier framework had cut US tariffs on Indian goods from as high as 50% to 18% before a Supreme Court ruling forced a rework.

US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said the United States and India are very close to concluding a bilateral trade agreement, with the broad framework settled and negotiators working through remaining detail. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on Thursday, he said major issues had been resolved after about a year and a half of talks.

"The big picture, the big framework, the big items are done."

— Sergio Gor, US Ambassador to India

The remarks are the newest development in the talks, building on External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's comment earlier this week that the two sides were heading toward a landing point. Gor's update adds two specifics that were not in that earlier assessment: the negotiations have reached line-by-line tariff discussion, and a linked decision on Russian energy sanctions is now days away.

Down to percentages

Gor said he had sat in negotiating rooms with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal where officials were, in his description, discussing percentages for individual products. That level of detail, he argued, reflects the scale of the two economies rather than a breakdown. He declined to set a date or identify what remains unresolved, and acknowledged that new issues, including changes in technology, had emerged as the talks lengthened.

According to Forbes India, Gor also explained why an earlier framework required reworking. India faced tariffs as high as 50% at one point last year, brought down to 18% when a framework was announced in February, within weeks of his arrival. A US Supreme Court ruling that the tariff authority was unconstitutional then required the administration to revisit parts of that arrangement.

The Russian oil question

Running alongside the trade talks is new US legislation that gives President Donald Trump authority to impose tariffs of as much as 100% on countries buying Russian oil and gas. Gor told the forum, as reported by The Times of India, that Trump must make a determination within the law's 30-day window, which he put at roughly the next 10 days. No country has yet been sanctioned under the law, and Gor said any exemption or relief for India would be a presidential decision.

He stressed the measure was not written to target India. The law, which he noted passed the Senate with 86 votes, covers three categories — oil purchases, gas purchases and sanctions evasion — and India falls into one of them alongside many other countries. Its stated purpose, he said, is to increase pressure on Russia to end the war in Ukraine, not to punish buyers. India has repeatedly defended buying energy from any source on grounds of energy security for its 1.4 billion people.

Why the pace matters

Gor contrasted the 18-month US negotiation with India's trade agreement with the European Union, concluded earlier this year after roughly 20 years of talks. He called the current pace unusually fast for an agreement of this complexity and said he was confident a deal would be reached.

He also pointed to cross-investment as evidence the relationship extends beyond tariffs, citing defence co-production in India and data centre and semiconductor investment by Google, Microsoft, Adobe and Micron. Jobs created in India, he argued, support counterpart jobs in the United States.

What to watch

Two clocks now matter. The first is Trump's determination on the Russian energy law, expected within days, which will clarify whether Indian oil purchases draw penalties or relief. The second is whether Greer and Goyal can close the remaining product-level items Gor described without new issues reopening settled parts of the framework. Until a text is announced, exporters should treat the 18% framework rate as provisional rather than final.
